titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§170–171: Jamuqa's Warning, and the Battle
about: Two sections. Chinggis Qahan, warned by the herdsmen, breaks camp in the night and, on the next day, sees the dust of Wang Qan's army coming. In §170 Wang Qan asks Jamuqa which of Temüjin's men are fighters, lays out his order of battle, and puts Jamuqa in command of the army; Jamuqa sends word secretly to Chinggis with the whole plan. In §171 Jürchedei and Quildar take the vanguard, the two armies meet, and the first day's fighting ends with Senggum shot in the cheek and Chinggis's men camping apart. Many passages are marked in the notes as first readings.

sentences.t: Tein ügülegdežü Čiṅgis Qaγan Badai, Kišiliγ qojar-un üges büširežü
sentences.l: So being-told, Čiṅgis Qaγan, Badai, Kišiliγ, two-of words believing,
sentences.i: So, being told, Chinggis Qahan believed the words of the two, Badai and Kishiliq.
sentences.n: ügülegdežü is ügüle- 'speak' + passive -gde- + converb -žü, 'being told' (Ming 被說着): the word has come to him from the two herdsmen of §169. büširežü is 'believing' (Ming 信着; the stem büšire- is inferred from the Ming). qojar-un üges is 'of-the-two words', the numeral taking the genitive and the plural -s on üge, with the possessor before the noun as always. Watch the converb chain begin here: this unit and the next hang on one finite verb, ködölbe, at unit 3.

sentences.t: süni böġed dergedeġün bükün itegelten-e kelen kiġed
sentences.l: Night indeed, near being reliable-ones-to, word having-said,
sentences.i: That same night he told those near him whom he could rely on,
sentences.n: süni böġed is 'night indeed' (Ming 夜裏 便); böġed here works as a particle of sequence, 'then, just then'. dergedeġün bükün (Ming 附近 有的) is 'those being near'; both words are uncertain in form, and I take them together as 'those who were close by'. itegelten-e: itegel 'trust, support' + -ten 'those having' + dative-locative -e (Ming 可倚仗的(每)行), 'to those who can be relied on'. This is the possessive/having pattern (-tü, -tan, -ten) in its plural; it comes back below in tuγtan and serelten. kelen kiġed is 'word having made', the idiom for 'having spoken' (Ming 話 說了); kiġed is ki- 'do, make' + -ġed.

morph.gloss: converb ending, here a particle of sequence: then, indeed (uncertain)
near, close by (form uncertain, read from the Ming 附近) [附近]
trust, support (from itege- 'rely') [可倚仗的(每)行]
to do, make (kelen ki- 'to speak') [說了]

sentences.t: küṅgelen jaγ̇u-ke-ben geġed burulan süni böġed ködölbe.
sentences.l: Lightly, whatever-things-his-own having-cast-off, hiding, night indeed set-out.
sentences.i: Travelling light, leaving all his gear behind and keeping out of sight, he set out that very night.
sentences.n: A rough unit; the Ming glosses are all I have. küṅgelen is 'light' (Ming 輕); jaγ̇u-ke-ben is jaγ̇u 'what' + ke 'thing' (my reading of Ming 甚麽物等, 'whatever things') + reflexive-possessive -ben, 'whatever of his own'. geġed is 'having cast off' (Ming 弃了), a stem geġe- inferred from the Ming; burulan is 'hiding' (Ming 躱着), also inferred. The sense, 'slipping away without baggage', is a guess from the Ming. ködölbe, past of ködöl- 'move, set out', is the finite verb that closes the chain begun two units back.

morph.gloss: thing, stuff (reading from the Ming 物等, uncertain)
to cast off, abandon (stem inferred from the Ming 弃) [弃了]
to hide, avoid (stem inferred from the Ming 躱) [躱着]
converb ending, here a particle of sequence: then, indeed (uncertain)

sentences.t: Maγ̇u-Ündür-ün gerü-ġer ködölürün Maγ̇u-Ündür-ün gerü-de Urjaṅqadai Želme-Γoγ̇a-ji itegežü
sentences.l: Maγ̇u-Ündür-of shade-side-along moving-when, Maγ̇u-Ündür-of shade-side-in Uriangqadai Želme-Γoγ̇a-(object) relying,
sentences.i: As he moved along the shaded side of Ma'u-Ündür, he put his trust, on that shaded side, in Jelme-Qo'a of the Uriangqadai,
sentences.n: Maγ̇u-Ündür is a mountain (Ming 山名), 'Bad-High' by its parts. gerü is the back or shaded side (Ming 背陰); gerü-ġer, with -ġer 'along', then gerü-de, 'on the shaded side'. ködölürün is ködöl- + the converb of time -rün (Ming 動時), 'when moving'. Želme-Γoγ̇a-ji takes the accusative -ji (Ming 行), and itegežü, 'relying', is itege- + -žü (Ming 倚仗着), so he relies on Jelme-Qo'a; the clause runs on into the next unit. Urjaṅqadai is read 'of the Urjaṅqai', as the glossary has it, though the Ming labels it 種名, a tribe name.

morph.gloss: Ma'u-Ündür, name of a mountain (maγ̇u 'bad', ündür 'high') [山名 的]
back, the shaded side [背陰 依着]
Ma'u-Ündür, name of a mountain [山名 的]
back, the shaded side [背陰 行]
Uriangqadai, a man of the Urjaṅqai (Urjaṅqai + -dai, person of, suffix uncertain) [(種)名]

sentences.t: qoina-γ̇an čaγduγ̇ulsun bolγan qaraγ̇ulsun talbižu ködölžü
sentences.l: Rear-own rear-guard making, lookouts setting-down, moving,
sentences.i: and made his rear a rearguard, posted lookouts, and moved on.
sentences.n: qoina-γ̇an is 'behind' with the reflexive-possessive -γ̇an, 'his own rear' (Ming 後 自(的)行). čaγduγ̇ulsun (Ming 後哨) and qaraγ̇ulsun (Ming 哨望) look like causative stems with an ending -sun, 'the ones made to watch'; I read them as 'rear-scouts' and 'lookouts' and cannot name the ending. bolγan is bol- 'become' made causative, 'making … into'. Three converbs (bolγan, talbižu, ködölžü) pile up before the finite verb in the next unit; that is the Mongol chain again.

morph.gloss: to move, set in motion [動着]

sentences.t: tere ködölügseġer manaγarši üdür düli naran kelberiġürün Qara-Qalžid eled kürčü üderin baγ̇uba.
sentences.l: That having-moved-since, next-morning day noon sun slanting, Qara-Qalžid sands reaching, noon-resting dismounted.
sentences.i: Having moved on in this way, on the next day, as the noon sun began to slant, he reached the Qara-Qalchid Sands and dismounted for the midday rest.
sentences.n: ködölügseġer is the past participle -gsen with the instrumental -ġer, 'since having moved' (Ming 動了依着); tere is 'that'. manaγarši üdür düli naran kelberiġürün is Ming 明早 晝 午 日 斜, 'tomorrow-ward day noon sun slanting'; the stem of kelberiġürün is inferred from the Ming, so 'as the noon sun slanted' is my reading. Qara-Qalžid is a sand-tract (Ming 沙磧名), eled is 'sands' (Ming 沙磧; a plural in -d, but the stem el- is not the el 'peace' of the glossary, so its form is uncertain). üderin is 'resting at noon' (Ming 歇餉), and baγ̇uba, 'came down', is the usual verb for dismounting or halting.

morph.gloss: to move, set out [動了依着]
to slant, decline (stem inferred from the Ming 斜) [斜]
Qara-Qalchid, name of a sand-tract [沙磧名]
sand, sandy waste (Ming 沙磧; not el 'peace'; stem uncertain) [沙磧]
to rest at midday (Ming 歇餉) [歇餉]

sentences.t: Üderidčü büküi-dür Alčidai-jin Aγtas aduγ̇ulaγ̇ulsun Čigidai, Jadir žüile žüile noγoγ̇an-dur aγtas(i)-jan aduγ̇ulan jabuqui-dur
sentences.l: Noon-resting while-being, Alčidai-of geldings caused-to-herd, Čigidai, Jadir together together green-grass-in geldings-their-own herding, going-about-when,
sentences.i: While he rested at noon, Chigidai and Jadir, who had been set to herd Alchidai's geldings, were herding their geldings together on the green grass, and as they went about,
sentences.n: A long suspended clause, kept whole because its subject, Čigidai and Jadir, is named only in the middle. Üderidčü is üderi- 'rest at noon' + converb; the form -dčü is the converb -čü after a stem in -i (it comes again at unit 31 in böldeidčü). aduγ̇ulaγ̇ulsun (Ming 敎放牧的) is aduγ̇ula- 'herd' + causative + -sun, 'those made to herd'; whether Alčidai is the owner or the officer in charge the text does not say. žüile žüile (Ming 一路 一路) is printed twice, 'together, in company'. aγtas(i)-jan is the reflexive-possessive on 'geldings', 'their own' (presumably the geldings in their charge). jabuqui-dur is the participle with dative-locative, 'at the going about, while going'.

sentences.t: qoināča Maγ̇u-Ündür-ün ebür(i)-jer Hulaγ̇an-Buruγad daγ̇arin aisuqui dain-u toγ̇usun-i üžežü dain kürbe.
sentences.l: From-behind Maγ̇u-Ündür-of front-along Hulaγ̇an-Buruγad passing, coming enemy-of dust-(object) seeing, enemy arrived.
sentences.i: they saw the dust of an enemy coming from behind, along the front of Ma'u-Ündür and past Hula'an-Buruqad: "The enemy has come!"
sentences.n: qoināča is qoina 'behind' + ablative -ča, 'from behind'. ebür is 'front' (Ming 前), set against the gerü 'back' of the mountain above; -jer is an ending with the shape of the instrumental, 'along' (Ming 依着), and Shiratori's (i) is a linking vowel. Hulaγ̇an-Buruγad is a place (Ming 地名). daγ̇arin is 'passing' (Ming 經過). aisuqui dain-u toγ̇usun-i is 'coming enemy's dust', the participle aisuqui qualifying the dust. The last two words, dain kürbe, are the herdsmen's cry, 'the enemy has arrived'; keġežü, 'saying', follows in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Ma'u-Ündür, name of a mountain [山名 的]
front, the near side (Ming 前) [前 依着]
ending with the shape of an instrumental: along, by way of (Ming 依着)
Hula'an-Buruqad, a place name (hulaγ̇an 'red', Ming 地名) [地名]
to pass by, go through (Ming 經過) [經過]

sentences.t: keġežü aγtans(i)-jan hüldeġed irežü
sentences.l: Saying, geldings-their-own having-chased, coming.
sentences.i: So saying, they drove their geldings before them and came.
sentences.n: keġežü closes the cry of the last unit ('saying'). hüldeġed is hülde- 'chase, drive' + -ġed 'having …ed' (Ming 趕了); here the sense is 'driving on ahead of them'. irežü, 'coming', then hangs the whole on the verb of the next unit. The print has aγtans(i)-jan, with an extra n, for aγtas(i)-jan.

sentences.t: dain kürbe.
sentences.l: Enemy arrived.
sentences.i: "The enemy has come!"
sentences.n: The same cry, dain kürbe, is repeated as the herdsmen's report to Chinggis; Shiratori closes it with a full stop. kürbe is kür- 'reach, arrive' + past -be. After this the Mongol turns to what Chinggis did on being told.

sentences.t: keġegdežü üžeġesü Maγ̇u-Ündür-ün ebür(i)- jer Hulaγ̇an-Buruγad daγ̇arin toγ̇osun γarγažu
sentences.l: Being-told, when-looking, Maγ̇u-Ündür-of front-along Hulaγ̇an-Buruγad passing, dust raising,
sentences.i: Told this, he looked: along the front of Ma'u-Ündür, past Hula'an-Buruqad, dust was being raised,
sentences.n: keġegdežü is keġe- 'say' + passive -gde- + -žü, 'being told' (Ming 被說着), and üžeġesü is üže- 'see' + the conditional converb -ġesü, 'when he looked' (Ming 看呵). Then the same path as in unit 8. γarγažu is γar- 'go out' + causative -γa- + -žu, 'making go out, raising'; the Ming has 望着 'looking toward', which does not fit, so I follow the grammar and read 'raising dust'. toγ̇osun is a variant of toγ̇usun, 'dust'.

morph.gloss: Ma'u-Ündür, name of a mountain [山名 的]
ending with the shape of an instrumental: along, by way of [依着]
to pass by, go through [經過]
converb: raising, making go out (the Ming 望 'looking' does not fit)

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān tere nekežü aisun ažuγ̇ui keġežü
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān that raiding coming was, saying,
sentences.i: "That is Wang Qan, coming to attack," he said.
sentences.n: nekežü is 'attacking' (Ming 襲着; the stem neke- is not secure). aisun ažuγ̇ui is aisu- 'come' + the ending -n with a- 'be' in the past -žuγ̇ui, 'was coming' (Ming 來 有來); the Ming's past tense is probably a past of report, not a past of time, since the enemy is still approaching. tere is 'that one'. The speaker is not named; the context makes Chinggis likely, and keġežü is only 'saying'.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (personal name) [人名]
to attack, raid (stem uncertain, Ming 襲) [襲着]

sentences.t: tendēče Čiṅgis Qaγan toγ̇osun üžeġed aγtas(i)-jan bariγ̇uluγ̇ad ačaγ̇alažu morilaba.
sentences.l: From-there Čiṅgis Qaγan dust having-seen, geldings-their-own having-caused-to-seize, loading, mounted.
sentences.i: Thereupon Chinggis Qahan, seeing the dust, had his geldings caught, loaded them, and mounted.
sentences.n: tendēče is tende 'there' + ablative with a long vowel, 'from there', used as 'thereupon'. bariγ̇uluγ̇ad is bari- 'seize' + causative -γ̇ul- + -uγ̇ad, 'having had (them) seized' (Ming 敎拿來). ačaγ̇alažu is 'loading' (Ming 䭾䭾着, to carry on the back); the stem is inferred, and what is loaded is not said, so 'them' is my filling in. morilaba is morila- 'mount', from morin 'horse'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin [太祖︀]
to load on, to carry on the back (stem inferred from the Ming 䭾) [䭾䭾着]
to mount a horse (from morin 'horse') [上馬了]

sentences.t: Tedüi ese üžeġesü gened büleġei.
sentences.l: Those not if-seeing, unawares there-was.
sentences.i: Had he not seen them then, it would have come on him unawares.
sentences.n: A hard sentence; this is a guess at the sense. tedüi is taken as the pronoun 'those' (Ming 那些), the object of üžeġesü, as the glossary has it; ese is 'not' for a past act, and with the conditional üžeġesü it makes 'if he had not seen'. gened (Ming 不意, 'unexpectedly') is an adverb whose form I cannot analyse. büleġei is bü- 'be' in the past -leġei, 'there was' (Ming 有來). I read the whole as a remark of the narrator: had he not seen them, the attack would have been a surprise.

morph.gloss: those, so many (pronoun; Ming 那些) [那些]
suddenly, unawares (Ming 不意, form uncertain) [不意]

sentences.t: Tere aisuqui-dur Žamuqa Waṅ-Qān-luγ̇a qamtu aisulčažu aisun ažuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: That coming-at, Žamuqa Waṅ-Qān-with together coming-together coming had-been.
sentences.i: At that time Jamuqa had come together with Wang Qan, in company.
sentences.n: tere aisuqui-dur is 'at that coming' (Ming 那 來的 時). Waṅ-Qān-luγ̇a has the comitative -luγ̇a (Ming 一同), 'together with Wang Qan'. aisulčažu is aisu- 'come' with -lča- 'together' (Ming 共來着) + -žu; with qamtu 'together' this says twice that they came in company. aisun ažuγ̇ui, 'had been coming', is as in unit 12. So Jamuqa is on the other side again, riding with Wang Qan.

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名 一同]

sentences.t: Tende Waṅ-Qān Žamuqa- dāča asaγčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: There Waṅ-Qān Žamuqa-from asked.
sentences.i: There Wang Qan questioned Jamuqa.
sentences.n: Žamuqa- is printed with a hyphen and the ablative dāča (Ming 荅察, 行) set as its own word; -dāča is the ablative, here 'from', the usual way to say 'ask of someone'. The long ā is Shiratori's. asaγčuγ̇u is asaγ- 'ask' + the past -čuγ̇u (Ming 問有來), the form of -žuγ̇u after a consonant. This sentence states the question; the next unit gives it in his words.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]
Jamuqa, a man's name (hyphen: the ablative follows as its own word) [人名]
ablative: from (long ā, as in ask 'from' someone) [行]

sentences.t: "Temüžin köġün-dür qadqulduqun metüs ked bi" keġen asaγčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: "Temüžin son-at fighting-ones kinds who are?" saying, had-asked.
sentences.i: "Among the son Temüjin's people, who are there of the sort that fight?" he asked.
sentences.n: A quotation that Shiratori opens at Temüžin and closes at bi. köġün-dür is köġün 'son' + dative-locative (Ming 子 行); Wang Qan is speaking of Temüjin as a son, but the Ming also glosses dür only as 行, so 'among the son Temüjin's' is a free rendering of the dative. qadqulduqun is qadqu- + reciprocal -ldu- + participle -qun, 'those who fight' (Ming 厮殺的); metüs is 'the sort, kinds' (Ming 般每). ked is 'who' in the plural (Ming 誰每); bi is 'are'. keġen … asaγčuγ̇u is 'saying … asked'.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名]
dative-locative: to, at, in the case of (front-vowel form)
to fight (stem inferred, Ming 厮殺) [厮殺︀的]
like, of the sort (postposition; Ming 般) [般每]

sentences.t: Žamuqa ügülerün:" Tende Uruγ̇ud Moṅγud keġen irgen in-ü bi.
sentences.l: Žamuqa saying: "There Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud saying people his are."
sentences.i: Jamuqa answered: "There are the people called the Uruqud and the Mongqud; they are his.
sentences.n: tende is 'there', in the sense of 'among them'. Uruγ̇ud and Moṅγud are tribal names (Ming 種(名)); keġen here is 'saying' as 'called'. irgen is 'people, the folk of a camp' (Ming 百姓), and in-ü after it is the third-person genitive 'his', set after its noun. bi is again 'are', with the noun first and no copula in the l.

morph.gloss: the Uruqud, a people (Ming 種名) [種(名)]
the Mongqud, a people (Ming 種名) [種(名)]
people, the folk of a camp [百姓]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: Tede irgen in-ü qadquldumui- že
sentences.l: Those people his fighting-are indeed.
sentences.i: Those, his people, are fighters indeed.
sentences.n: qadquldumui is qadqu- + reciprocal -ldu- + the present -mui, 'fight' (Ming 厮殺有); že is a particle 'indeed' (Ming 也者) and is hyphenated to the verb in print. tede is the plural 'those'.

sentences.t: Toγ̇oriqui tutum toγ̇i žokiju; derelgükü tutum-den žokiju.
sentences.l: Turning-when each-time formation fitting-is; reversing each-time in-order fitting-is.
sentences.i: Whenever they wheel, their formation is right each time; whenever they turn about, it is right in order each time.
sentences.n: The sense is a praise of their drill, and the stems are uncertain. toγ̇oriqui (Ming 轉時) is 'when turning' with the participle -qui; derelgükü (Ming 翻旋時) is 'when reversing', its stem uncertain; tutum is 'each time' (Ming 每遍), toγ̇i 'battle array' (Ming 陣勢). žokiju is žoki- 'be fitting' (Ming 宜) + the present -ju. tutum-den adds -den (Ming 次序, 'order'), which I translate as 'in order' without being sure of the ending.

morph.gloss: to turn, circle (stem uncertain, Ming 轉) [轉時]
battle array, formation (Ming 陣勢) [陣勢]
to be fitting, suitable (Ming 宜) [宜有]
to turn over, wheel about (stem uncertain, Ming 翻旋) [翻旋時]
each, every time [每遍 次序]
ending of uncertain force: in order (Ming 次序)

sentences.t: Üčügen-eče üldü žida-dur daduγsan irgen.
sentences.l: Little-from sword spear-in accustomed people.
sentences.i: They are a people accustomed from childhood to sword and lance.
sentences.n: Üčügen-eče is üčügen 'small' + ablative -eče, 'from small', Ming 從小. üldü is 'sword' (Ming 刀; as printed), žida-dur 'in the spear' with dative-locative (Ming 鎗 裏). daduγsan is dadu- 'be used to' + past participle -γsan, 'those who have become used' (Ming 慣了的). irgen is the head noun, so the participle phrase precedes it: possessor-and-modifier before noun again.

morph.gloss: to be accustomed (Ming 慣) [慣了的]

sentences.t: Tede qaraγčiγ̇ud, alaγčiγ̇ud tuγtan bi.
sentences.l: Those black-ones, dappled-ones standard-having are.
sentences.i: They are the black ones and the dappled ones, men with standards.
sentences.n: These three words are doubtful. qaraγčiγ̇ud (Ming 黑每) and alaγčiγ̇ud (Ming 花每) are 'black ones' and 'dappled ones', plurals in -γčiγ̇ud; whether these are troop names or descriptions of the horses or banners I cannot say. tuγtan is tuγ 'standard' + -tan 'those having' (the plural of -tu; Ming 旄纛(有的)每), as in itegelten above.

morph.gloss: standard, banner (Ming 旄纛) [旄纛(有的)每]

sentences.t: Tede serelten irgen bi-že" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Those ones-to-be-guarded-against people are-indeed, saying-said.
sentences.i: They are a people to be wary of," he said.
sentences.n: serelten is serel 'caution' + -ten 'those having', with the Ming 可防的(每), 'those to be guarded against'; the likeness to itegelten is deliberate. bi-že is bü- 'be' in the stem bi- before the particle -že (Ming 有也者). The quotation ends at bi-že"; keġežüġüi is keġe- + the past -žüġüi, 'said', the front-vowel form of -žuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: wariness, caution (from sere- 'be alert') [可防的(每)]

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: That word-in Waṅ-Qān saying:
sentences.i: At these words Wang Qan said:
sentences.n: üge-dür is 'in the word, at the word' (Ming 言語 裏), dative-locative -dür after a front-vowel stem. ügülerün is the converb of time, 'saying'. The speech that follows is Wang Qan's plan of battle.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]

sentences.t: "Tein böġesü bida teden-dür Žirgin baγ̇atud(i)-jan Qadag-i tušijaldun Žirgin baγ̇atud(i)-jan dobtulγaja
sentences.l: "So if-be, we them-to Žirgin heroes-own Qadag-(object) facing, Žirgin heroes-own let-us-make-charge.
sentences.i: "If so, against them let us send in our own Jirgin heroes, with Qadaq set to face them, our own Jirgin heroes charging.
sentences.n: tein böġesü is 'so, if it be', the conditional of bü- (Ming 那般 有來). bida is the inclusive 'we' (Ming 咱). baγ̇atud(i)-jan is 'heroes' with the reflexive-possessive, 'our own', printed twice. The hard part is Qadag-i tušijaldun: Qadag is a man's name (Ming 人名) in the accusative, and tušijaldun is tuši- 'face' + a reciprocal ending (Ming 相對, 'facing each other'); I cannot be sure whether Qadaq leads the Jirgin or is matched against someone, so the English leaves it loose. dobtulγaja is dobtul- 'charge' + causative -γa- + -ja, 'let us have (them) charge' (Ming 敎衝咱), the exhortation ending that returns in every clause of the plan.

morph.gloss: that, they (plural tede, here stem teden-) [他每行]
Jirgin, a people (Ming 姓名) [姓(名)]
hero, brave warrior [勇士(每)自的行]
Qadaq, a man's name (personal name) [人名行]
to face, meet (Ming 相對) [相對]
hero, brave warrior [勇士(每)自的行]

sentences.t: Žirgin-u gežige Tümen-Tübegen-ü Ačiγ-Širun-i dobtulγaja.
sentences.l: Žirgin-of reserve, Tümen-Tübegen-of Ačiγ-Širun-(object) let-us-make-charge.
sentences.i: For the Jirgin's reserve, let us send in Achiq-Shirun of the Tümen-Tübegen.
sentences.n: gežige is 'reserve, rear support' (Ming 後援); Shiratori prints it after its genitive, 'Žirgin-u gežige', the possessor first. Tümen-Tübegen and Žirgin are tribal names (Ming 姓(名)的, i.e. 'of the clan'); Ačiγ-Širun is a man (Ming 人名). The accusative -i marks him as the one made to charge, as with the -ja ending.

morph.gloss: Tümen-Tübegen, a clan name (Ming 姓名) [姓(名)的]
Achiq-Shirun, a man's name (personal name) [人名行]

sentences.t: Tübegen-i gežige Olon-Doṅγaid baγ̇atud-i dobtulγaja.
sentences.l: Tübegen-(of?) reserve, Olon-Doṅγaid heroes-(object) let-us-make-charge.
sentences.i: For the Tübegen's reserve, let us send in the heroes of the Olon-Dongqaid.
sentences.n: Tübegen-i is printed with -i and glossed by the Ming as a genitive (姓(名)的), as if 'of the Tübegen'; I follow the Ming, because an accusative here would leave gežige without an owner. The Olon-Doṅγaid are another clan (Ming 姓(名)), the Toṅγaid of the earlier part printed here with D; the English keeps Shiratori's D, baγ̇atud-i the heroes as the ones sent in. Recurring pattern of the speech: each division is named, then its reserve.

morph.gloss: ending glossed as genitive by the Ming (printed -i, uncertain)
Olon-Dongqaid, a clan name (Ming 姓名) [姓(名)]
hero, brave warrior [勇士每 行]

sentences.t: Doṅγaid-un gežige Waṅ-Qān-(n)u miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-i uduridun Qori-Šilemün-Taiži dobtultuγai.
sentences.l: Doṅγaid-of reserve, Waṅ-Qān-of thousand guards-(object) leading, Qori-Šilemün-Taiži let-him-charge.
sentences.i: For the Dongqaid's reserve, let Qori-Shilemün Taiji lead Wang Qan's Thousand Guards in the charge.
sentences.n: uduridun is 'leading' (Ming 敎統着, with 敎 as causative: 'having him lead'); the stem uduri- is inferred and the ending -dun uncertain. turγaγ̇ud-i is the 'guards, followers' (Ming 護衞(每)) as object. Qori-Šilemün-Taiži is a man with the title taiži, 'prince' (Ming 人名). dobtultuγai is the optative -tuγai, 'let him charge' (Ming 敎衝者), the third-person counterpart of the 'let us' form above.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名的]
bodyguard, follower (Ming 護衞) [護衞(每)行]
to lead, command (stem inferred from the Ming 統) [敎統着]
Qori-Shilemün Taiji, a man's name with the title taiži 'prince' (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: Miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-un gežige bida jeke γol dobtulai-že keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Thousand guards-of reserve, we great centre let-us-charge indeed, saying-said.
sentences.i: And as the reserve of the Thousand Guards, we will charge as the great main body," he said.
sentences.n: miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-un is 'the Thousand of the guards' (Ming 千 護衞(每)的). γol is 'centre', the spine of a battle line (Ming 中軍). dobtulai-že is dobtul- + -ai + -že (Ming 衝 也者), 'we will charge indeed'; -ai I take as a first-person intention form. The speech ends here; Shiratori closes no quotation mark.

morph.gloss: centre, main body (Ming 中軍, elsewhere 'spine') [中軍]

sentences.t: Basa Waṅ-Qān ügülerün: "Žamuqa deġü bidan-u čerig či žasa" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Again Waṅ-Qān saying: "Žamuqa younger-brother, us-of army you set-in-order," saying-said.
sentences.i: Wang Qan spoke again: "Jamuqa, younger brother, take our army in hand," he said.
sentences.n: deġü, 'younger brother', stands as address (Ming 弟); Wang Qan calls Jamuqa deġü as a form of address. bidan-u is the genitive of bida, 'of us'. žasa is the bare verb stem used as an imperative, 'put in order, command' (Ming 整治); či, 'you', makes the person plain. Recurring pattern: a bare stem is a command, no ending.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]
to put in order, command (bare stem: imperative) [整治]

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Žamuqa öre böldeidčü γarču nököd-teġen ügülerün:
sentences.l: That word-in Žamuqa aside solitary-being going-out, companions-to-own saying:
sentences.i: At those words Jamuqa withdrew apart, and going out to his own companions, said:
sentences.n: öre is printed with a rare character in the Ming (𠮠), and I have it as 'aside, apart', which suits böldeidčü (Ming 孤零, 'solitary'; stem inferred, converb in -dčü as above). The glossary has öre as 'heart' and that may be right in some places; here it does not fit. nököd-teġen is nökör 'companion' + plural -d + dative -te + reflexive-possessive -ġen, 'to his own companions' (Ming 伴當每 自的行).

morph.gloss: aside, apart (Ming 𠮠, sense uncertain, elsewhere 'heart') [𠮠]
to be solitary, alone (stem inferred from the Ming 孤零) [孤零]
converb: -ing (-čü after an i-stem, with d)

sentences.t: "Waṅ-Qān ene čerig(i)-jen nama-ji žasa keġemü.
sentences.l: "Waṅ-Qān this army-own me-(object) set-in-order saying-is.
sentences.i: "Wang Qan says that I am to put this army of his in order.
sentences.n: nama-ji is the oblique stem nama- of bi 'I' + accusative -ji (Ming 行); the Ming 敎我整治 has the causative sense 'having me set in order', so the accusative marks the person given the task. čerigi-jen is čerig 'army' + the reflexive-possessive 'his own'. keġemü is keġe- 'say' + present -mü (Ming 說有). Jamuqa is reporting what he has just been told.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]
to put in order, command [整治]

sentences.t: Anda-dur bi qadquldun jadan jabuluγ̇a.
sentences.l: Anda-to I fighting-together being-unable was-going.
sentences.i: I have gone on, unable to fight my anda.
sentences.n: anda-dur is the anda, 'sworn brother', in the dative-locative (Ming 契交 行), and the anda is Temüjin. qadquldun is 'fighting one another' with the converb -n; jadan is jada- 'be unable' + -n (Ming 不能). jabuluγ̇a is jabu- 'go about' + -luγ̇a (Ming 行來), a past of continuing action, 'was going on, kept on'. I do not know the exact shape of the ending, and the gloss is the Ming's.

morph.gloss: sworn brother, pledged friend [契交 行]

sentences.t: Ene čerig nama-ji žasa keġemüi.
sentences.l: This army me-(object) set-in-order saying-is.
sentences.i: He says this army is for me to put in order.
sentences.n: A short repeat of unit 32, with keġemüi for keġemü, the same present in its fuller form.

morph.gloss: to put in order, command [整治]

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān deled na-dāča činaru ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān more me-than that-side was.
sentences.i: Wang Qan is farther off still than I.
sentences.n: The Mongol is terse. deled (Ming 越, 'more') is an adverb; na-dāča is 'than me', with the ablative (Ming 比我); činaru is 'that way, farther on' (Ming 那廂). I take Jamuqa to be saying that Wang Qan stands further from Temüjin than he does himself. This is a guess from the Ming; I could be wrong about whose side the 'far side' is. ažuγ̇u, 'was', is the past of a- 'be'.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]
more, all the more (Ming 越, form uncertain) [越]
further on, on that side [那廂]

sentences.t: Čaγtu nökör bijü.
sentences.l: Moderate companion there-is.
sentences.i: There is a companion who keeps the middle way.
sentences.n: Čaγtu is Ming 酌中, 'moderate, in the middle'; I take it as an adjective from čaγ 'time' + -tu 'having', but that analysis is only a guess, and the same words come again in unit 47. Jamuqa seems to be presenting himself as the one who stands between the two parties; the Mongol does not say 'I'. bijü is bü- 'be' in the present form bijü (Ming 有).

morph.gloss: moderate, in the middle (Ming 酌中, čaγ 'time' + -tu, uncertain) [酌中]

sentences.t: Anda-dur kele oroγ̇uluja. Anda qadaγ̇učituγai."
sentences.l: Anda-to word let-me-cause-to-enter. Anda be-on-guard-let."
sentences.i: Let me pass word to my anda: let my anda be on his guard."
sentences.n: oroγ̇uluja is oro- 'enter' + causative -γ̇ul- + -ja, 'let me put in', i.e. 'let me convey' (Ming 敎入咱). qadaγ̇učituγai is qadaγ̇uči- 'be careful, on guard' (Ming 敎戒愼着; compare 謹愼 at unit 51) + the optative -tuγai, 'let him …'. The quotation closes with the full stop after it.

morph.gloss: sworn brother, pledged friend [契交 行]
to be on guard, careful (Ming 謹愼) [敎戒愼着]

sentences.t: keġežü Žamuqa doloγ̇un Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur kele oroγ̇ulžu ügüležü ilerün;
sentences.l: Saying, Žamuqa secretly Čiṅgis Qaγan-to word causing-to-enter, speaking, sending:
sentences.i: So saying, Jamuqa secretly sent word to Chinggis Qahan, speaking thus:
sentences.n: doloγ̇un is 'secretly' (Ming 暗地). oroγ̇ulžu is the causative converb of oro-, 'making enter'; ügüležü is 'speaking'; ilerün is ile- 'send' with -rün, but the Ming glosses it 去 'go' and not 敎去, so 'sending' is a decision; elsewhere I have kept ile- as 'send'. The message that follows is quoted by Jamuqa.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Waṅ-Qān na-dāča asaγba.
sentences.l: "Waṅ-Qān me-from asked.
sentences.i: "Wang Qan questioned me.
sentences.n: The quotation of the message opens here; it is Jamuqa's message to Chinggis and runs to the end of the section. na-dāča is bi 'I' (stem na-) + ablative -dāča, 'from me' (Ming 比我 earlier, here 我行). asaγba is asaγ- 'ask' + past -ba.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]

sentences.t: Temüžin köġün- dür qadqulduqun metüs ked bi keġen asaγasuγ̇asu bi ügülerün:
sentences.l: Temüžin son-of fighting-ones kinds who are, saying when-asked, I saying:
sentences.i: When he asked, 'Among the son Temüjin's people, who are there of the sort that fight?' I said:
sentences.n: Temüžin köġün-dür … keġen is the same question as at unit 17, with the Ming now glossing dür 的(處), 'of, at' (so 'in the matter of the son Temüjin'). asaγasuγ̇asu is asaγa- 'ask' + conditional -γ̇asu 'when' (Ming 問呵, 'when asked'); the -su- inside it I cannot account for. bi is 'I', the pronoun. ügülerün is 'saying'; the speech follows.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to, at, of (front-vowel form) [的(處)]
conditional converb: if, when (the -su- inside is unaccounted for)

sentences.t: Uruγ̇ud Moṅγud-i tumbulan ügülebe. bi.
sentences.l: Uruγ̇ud Moṅγud-(object) heading spoke I.
sentences.i: I named the Uruqud and the Mongqud first.
sentences.n: tumbulan is 'taking as head, putting first' (Ming 爲頭), the stem tumbula- inferred; the Uruγ̇ud and Moṅγud-i are its objects. ügülebe is ügüle- + -be, 'spoke'. The pronoun bi sits after the verb, 'spoke I'.

morph.gloss: to take as head, put first (stem inferred from the Ming 爲頭) [爲頭]

sentences.t: Min-u üge-dür müd Žirgin(i)-jan tumbulažu maṅlailan žasalduba.
sentences.l: My-of word-in they Žirgin-own heading, vanguard-making, were-set-in-order.
sentences.i: By my word they made their own Jirgin their head, and drew up as the vanguard.
sentences.n: Min-u is 'my', the genitive of bi (stem min-), and it comes before üge. müd is 'they' (Ming 他每; uncertain form). tumbulažu is 'heading' (Ming 爲頭着). maṅlailan is maṅlai 'forehead, front' (Ming 爲頭, 'at the head') + -la- 'act as' + -n, so 'being the vanguard'. žasalduba is žasa- 'put in order' + -ldu- + past -ba (Ming 整治了), 'were drawn up'. The ‘they’ are the Kereid, whose plan Jamuqa is reporting, set against what he told Wang Qan.

morph.gloss: Jirgin, a people [姓(名) 自的行]
forehead, front, van (Ming 爲頭) [爲頭]

sentences.t: Žirgin-u gežige Tümen-Tübegen-ü Ačiγ-Širun-i keġeldübe.
sentences.l: Žirgin-of reserve, Tümen-Tübegen-of Ačiγ-Širun-(object) said-together.
sentences.i: As the Jirgin's reserve, they have agreed upon Achiq-Shirun of the Tümen-Tübegen.
sentences.n: keġeldübe is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- + past -be (Ming 共說了), 'they said it together, agreed'. Jamuqa now recites to Chinggis, in the same words, the order of battle that Wang Qan gave in unit 25-29; a good place to check your grammar against the earlier lines.

sentences.t: Doṅγaid-un gežige Waṅ-Qān-(n)u miṅγan turγaγ̇ud-un nojan Qori-Šilemün-Taiži-ji keġeldübe.
sentences.l: Doṅγaid-of reserve, Waṅ-Qān-of thousand guards-of lord Qori-Šilemün-Taiži-(object) said-together.
sentences.i: As the Dongqaid's reserve, they have agreed upon Qori-Shilemün Taiji, the lord of Wang Qan's Thousand Guards.
sentences.n: nojan is 'lord, commander' (Ming 官人). The Ming 其說了 for keġeldübe here is the same verb as before. The order now stands exactly as Wang Qan gave it.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名的]
Qori-Shilemün Taiji, a man's name with the title taiži 'prince' [人名 行]

sentences.t: Teġün-ü gežige mün Waṅ-Qān-(n)u jeke γol čerig(i)-jer baisu keġeldübe.
sentences.l: That-of reserve just Waṅ-Qān-of great centre army-with let-us-stand said-together.
sentences.i: And as the reserve of those, Wang Qan himself with the great main body of the army is to take his stand; so they have agreed.
sentences.n: Teġün-ü is tere 'that' in the stem teġün- + genitive -ü (Ming 他的). mün is 'just, the very' (Ming 只). čerig(i)-jer is čerig 'army' with an ending -jer, 'with the army' (Ming 軍(依着)). baisu is bai- 'stand' + the first-person ending -su, 'let us stand' (Ming 立咱). The 'let us' here is part of the agreed plan, and the two last words are Jamuqa's report.

morph.gloss: that, he (stem teġün- before case endings) [他的]
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名的]
ending with the shape of an instrumental: with

sentences.t: Basa Waṅ-Qān ügülerün: "Žamuqa deġü ene čerig či žasa keġen nama-ji tüšin ügülemüi.
sentences.l: Again Waṅ-Qān saying: "Žamuqa younger-brother, this army you set-in-order," saying, me-(object) entrusting says.
sentences.i: Wang Qan said again, 'Jamuqa, younger brother, take this army in hand,' and so he says, entrusting it to me.
sentences.n: A repeat of the command in unit 30, now inside Jamuqa's message. tüšin is tüši- 'entrust, rely on' (Ming 委付) + the converb -n; the stem I give is from the Ming. ügülemüi is ügüle- 'speak' + present -müi, 'says' (Ming 說有). The printed quotation marks are not closed in Shiratori's text between the two speeches.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]
to put in order, command (bare stem: imperative) [整治]
to entrust, depend on (stem inferred from the Ming 委付) [委付]

sentences.t: Eġü-ber uqaγ̇asu Čaγtu nökör bijü.
sentences.l: This-way-by if-understanding, moderate companion there-is.
sentences.i: If you take it so: there is a companion who keeps the middle way.
sentences.n: eġü-ber is 'by this way' (Ming 這般), the stem eġü uncertain; uqaγ̇asu is uqa- 'understand' + -γ̇asu 'if' (Ming 省呵). Čaγtu nökör bijü returns word for word from unit 36; I leave it as the glossary has it.

morph.gloss: this way (stem uncertain, Ming 這般) [這般]
moderate, in the middle (Ming 酌中) [酌中]

sentences.t: čerig(i)-jen žasaldun jaγ̇u čidaqun.
sentences.l: Army-own together setting-in-order, what able?
sentences.i: Ordering the army together, what can I do?
sentences.n: žasaldun is žasa- + reciprocal -ldu- + -n, 'ordering together' (Ming 共整治). čidaqun is čida- 'be able' + participle -qun (Ming 能的). I read the question as rhetorical, 'what can I accomplish?'; that is a guess about the tone, and 'together' is only the reciprocal -ldu-, with no one named.

sentences.t: Erte bi Anda-dur qadquldun jadažu jabuluγ̇a.
sentences.l: Formerly I anda-to fighting-together being-unable going-about-was.
sentences.i: Formerly I went on, unable to fight my anda.
sentences.n: erte is 'early, formerly' (Ming 在前). jadažu is jada- 'be unable' + -žu (Ming 不能着), and it hangs on the finite jabuluγ̇a, as in unit 33 but with a converb in place of -n. The unit says the same thing as unit 33 with different words, and I read it as a reaffirmation.

morph.gloss: sworn brother, pledged friend [契交 行]

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān na-dāča činaru ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān me-than that-side was.
sentences.i: Wang Qan is farther off than I.
sentences.n: The same sentence as unit 35, without deled 'more'. The Ming gives 比我 那廂 有; I carry over my doubt about the sense.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名]
further on, on that side [那廂]

sentences.t: Anda bu aju; qadaγ̇uži" keġežü iležügü.
sentences.l: Anda, do not fear; be-on-guard," saying, sent-off.
sentences.i: Anda, do not be afraid; be on your guard," he said, and sent the word off.
sentences.n: bu is the prohibitive particle 'do not' (Ming 休) before aju 'fear' (Ming 怕); the last, qadaγ̇uži, is a bare stem command (printed with ž, for the č of unit 37, I suppose) and glossed 謹愼. iležügü is ile- 'send' + the past -žügü (Ming 去了, 'went'); the Ming reading is that the word went off. The quotation of the message ends here, and the section with it.

morph.gloss: to fear, be afraid (bare stem used as a finite verb) [怕]
to be on guard, careful (variant of qadaγ̇uči-, bare stem: imperative) [謹︀愼]

sentences.t: Ene kele ireġülüġed Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:
sentences.l: This word having-caused-to-come, Čiṅgis Qaγan saying:
sentences.i: When this word had been brought to him, Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: ireġülüġed is ire- 'come' + causative -ġül- + -üġed, 'having caused to come, having had brought' (Ming (敎)來了). It carries the sense that the message was delivered. Ene kele is 'this word'; ügülerün introduces the speech.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Uruγ̇ud-un Žürčedei ebin či jaγ̇u keġemü. Čima-ji maṅlailaja" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Uruγ̇ud-of Žürčedei uncle, you what saying-are? You-(object) let-us-make-vanguard," said.
sentences.i: "Jürchedei of the Uruqud, uncle, what do you say? Let us make you the vanguard," he said.
sentences.n: ebin is 'uncle' (Ming 伯父, father's elder brother), used as a form of address and of respect. či jaγ̇u keġemü is 'you what say?' (keġemü, present). čima-ji is či in the oblique stem čima- + accusative -ji (Ming 你行). maṅlailaja is maṅlai + -la- 'act as' + -ja 'let us' (Ming 敎做先鋒), the same exhortation as in the battle plan above. The quotation closes at maṅlailaja", and keġebe is the past 'said'.

morph.gloss: Jürchedei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
uncle, father's elder brother (Ming 伯父) [伯父]

sentences.t: Žürčede-ji doṅγodqu-jin urida Moṅγud-un Quildar-Se- čen ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žürčede-(object) speaking-of before, Moṅγud-of Quildar-Sečen saying:
sentences.i: Before Jürchedei could speak up, Quildar Sechen of the Mongqud said:
sentences.n: A doubtful reading. doṅγodqu-jin is a participle 'the one who gives voice' + the genitive -jin (Ming 作聲的), and urida is 'before'; with the accusative on Žürčede-ji it means 'before Jürchedei's speaking'. Quildar-Se- čen are two words in print because the name Sečen ('wise') is broken at the end of a line; the second half carries no gloss from the Ming. Quildar is a man of the Mongqud (Ming 人名 and 姓(名)的), perhaps the Qujuldar of the Mongqud of an earlier part (printed there with 余 for 亦, so the vowels differ).

morph.gloss: Jürchedei, a man's name (stem Žürčede- before case) [人名 行]
to give voice, speak out (stem inferred from the Ming 作聲) [作聲的]
Quildar, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
first half of Sečen 'wise', broken across the line

sentences.t: "Anda-jin emüne bi qadquldusu.
sentences.l: "Anda-of before I let-me-fight.
sentences.i: "I will fight in front of my anda.
sentences.n: anda-jin has the genitive -jin after a vowel; emüne is 'in front' (Ming 前). qadquldusu is qadqu- + reciprocal -ldu- + the first-person ending -su, 'let me fight' (Ming 厮殺); the -su ending returns in unit 57 and in baisu earlier, and means 'let me / let us'.

morph.gloss: sworn brother, pledged friend [契交 的]

sentences.t: Mönö qoina önečid köġüd-i min-u asaraqu-ji anda medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Long after orphan sons-(object) my tending-(object) anda let-him-know," said.
sentences.i: In time to come, let my anda take heed of the raising of my orphaned sons," he said.
sentences.n: The Mongol is terse and I follow it closely. mönö qoina is Ming 久 後, 'long after, in time to come'; an earlier part has mönö qoina as 'from now on', and the glossary 'tomorrow' for mönö alone (Ming 明); here the Ming gives 久, so I read 'in time to come'. önečid köġüd-i is 'orphans, sons' as object, min-u 'my'. asaraqu-ji is asara- 'tend, raise' + participle -qu + accusative -ji (Ming 擡擧的 行). medetügei is mede- 'know' + optative -tügei, 'let him know' (Ming 知道者). The point is a vow to fight to the death and a request that the anda care for his children.

morph.gloss: long, for long; with qoina 'hereafter' (Ming 久; the glossary has 'tomorrow' from the Ming 明) [久]
to tend, care for, raise (Ming 擡擧) [擡擧的 行]

sentences.t: Žürčedei ügülerün: "Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-u emüne ba Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud maṅlailan qadquldusu" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Žürčedei saying: "Čiṅgis Qaγan-of before we Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud vanguard let-us-fight," saying-said.
sentences.i: Jürchedei said: "Before Chinggis Qahan, we, the Uruqud and the Mongqud, will fight as the vanguard," he said.
sentences.n: ba is 'we' (Ming 俺), set apart from bida 'we, inclusive' (Ming 咱); the Ming alternates 俺/咱 for the two; it stands at the head of its clause here. Qaγ̇an-u emüne is 'Qahan-of before'. maṅlailan qadquldusu is 'as vanguard, let us fight'. Both leaders thus take the front.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Tein kēġed Žürčedei Quildar qojar Uruγ̇ud Moṅγud(i)-jar(i)-jan Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-u emüne žasažu baiba.
sentences.l: So having-said, Žürčedei, Quildar, the-two Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud-with-own leading, Čiṅgis Qaγan-of before setting-in-order, stood.
sentences.i: Having said so, Jürchedei and Quildar, the two of them, leading their Uruqud and Mongqud, drew them up before Chinggis Qahan and took their stand.
sentences.n: kēġed is keġe- + -ġed with a long ē from the run-together stem (Ming 說了). qojar, 'two', follows the pair it counts. Moṅγud(i)-jar(i)-jan is Moṅγud with an accusative (i), the ending -jar and the reflexive-possessive -(i)jan; the Ming 領着 shows the sense, 'leading their own'. I attach Uruγ̇ud to Jürchedei and Moṅγud to Quildar as the Ming's two 姓 invite. žasažu is 'setting in order'; baiba is bai- 'stand' + past -ba.

morph.gloss: converb: having said (the stem and ending run together, written ē)
the Mongqud, a people [姓(名)領着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Baqui-luγ̇a dain Žirgin-i maṅlailažu kürčü irebe.
sentences.l: Stood-as-soon-as, enemy Žirgin-(object) vanguard-making, arriving came.
sentences.i: No sooner had they taken their stand than the enemy came on, making the Jirgin its vanguard.
sentences.n: Baqui-luγ̇a: Shiratori prints Baqui for baiqui, the participle of bai- 'stand'; -luγ̇a after a participle gives 'as soon as' (Ming 纔立了; compare ireküi-lüġe in the next unit). dain is 'enemy' (Ming (敵)). maṅlailažu is the verb maṅlaila- 'act as vanguard' with -žu, 'making (them) vanguard' (Ming 先鋒着). kürčü irebe is 'arriving came', a doubled verb of motion.

morph.gloss: as soon as (after a participle, uncertain)

sentences.t: ireküi-lüġe Uruγ̇ud Moṅγud esergü dobtulžu Žirgin-i daruba.
sentences.l: Coming-as-soon-as Uruγ̇ud, Moṅγud facing charging, Žirgin-(object) overcame.
sentences.i: As soon as they came, the Uruqud and the Mongqud charged to meet them and overcame the Jirgin.
sentences.n: ireküi-lüġe is ire- 'come' + participle -küi + -lüġe 'as soon as' (the same pattern as baqui-luγ̇a above); lüġe is the front-vowel form. esergü is 'facing, to meet' (Ming 迎着). dobtulžu is 'charging' (Ming 衝着). daruba is daru- 'overcome' + past (Ming 勝了), so the Jirgin were beaten and the chain closes.

morph.gloss: as soon as (after a participle, uncertain)

sentences.t: Daružu aisuqui-dur Tümen-Tübegen-ü Ačiγ-Širun dobtulba.
sentences.l: Having-overcome coming-when Tümen-Tübegen-of Ačiγ-Širun charged.
sentences.i: Having overcome them, as they pressed on, Achiq-Shirun of the Tümen-Tübegen charged.
sentences.n: Daružu aisuqui-dur is 'overcoming, at the coming', the next battle opening as the last closed. aisu- is the 'come' of the early parts, here used as 'advance'. The subject is Achiq-Shirun, the man named in the plan of unit 26. dobtulba is the past, 'charged'.

sentences.t: Dobtulžu Ačiγ-Širun Quildar-i qadqužu baγ̇ulžuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Charging Ačiγ-Širun Quildar-(object) thrusting-in, brought-down.
sentences.i: Charging, Achiq-Shirun thrust at Quildar and brought him down.
sentences.n: qadqužu is qadqu- 'thrust in, stab' + -žu (Ming 刺着, 'thrusting'), the same stem as in qadqul-, 'fight'. baγ̇ulžuγ̇u is baγ̇ul- 'cause to come down' (baγ̇u- 'descend' + causative -l-) + the past -žuγ̇u (Ming 落下了), 'unhorsed'. Quildar-i has the accusative.

morph.gloss: to thrust in, stab (Ming 刺) [刺着]
to bring down, unhorse (baγ̇u- 'descend' + causative -l-) [落下了]

sentences.t: Moṅγud Quildar-un deġere egeġerčüġüi.
sentences.l: Moṅγud Quildar-of on turned-over.
sentences.i: The Mongqud wheeled round over Quildar.
sentences.n: egeġerčüġüi is egeġerü- 'turn back, wheel about' (Ming 翻 'turn over'; an earlier part has egeġerüje, 'let us turn back', and the ü drops before the ending) + the past -čüġüi. 'Turned over on top of' is the Ming's picture; the context, a fallen leader, makes me take it as 'wheeled round over him', rallying about him. deġere here follows a genitive as 'on, over', like a postposition. The same verb returns in unit 71 for the Kereid round Senggum.

morph.gloss: to turn back, wheel about (Ming 翻 'turn over'; the ü drops before the ending) [翻了]

sentences.t: Žürčedei Uruγ̇ud(i)-jar(i)-jan dobtulžu Tümen-Tübegen-i daruba.
sentences.l: Žürčedei Uruγ̇ud-with-own leading charging, Tümen-Tübegen-(object) overcame.
sentences.i: Jürchedei, leading his Uruqud, charged and overcame the Tümen-Tübegen.
sentences.n: Uruγ̇ud(i)-jar(i)-jan is the Uruγ̇ud with the same -jar 'with, leading' as unit 58 for the Moṅγud. The Ming 姓(名)領着 means 'leading the tribe'. The Tümen-Tübegen are those of Achiq-Shirun. The unit is the second blow of Jürchedei's.

morph.gloss: the Uruqud, a people [姓(名) 領着]

sentences.t: Daružu ködölgežü aisuqui-dur Olon-Doṅγaid esergü dobtulba.
sentences.l: Having-overcome, setting-in-motion, coming-when Olon-Doṅγaid facing charged.
sentences.i: Having overcome them and driven them off, as he came on, the Olon-Dongqaid charged to meet him.
sentences.n: ködölgežü is ködöl- 'move' + causative -ge- + -žü, 'making move, setting in motion' (Ming 敎動着), here 'driving off'. The converb chain is: daružu, ködölgežü, then aisuqui-dur, with the next battle opening on a participle + -dur 'when' clause. esergü and dobtulba are as in unit 60.

morph.gloss: to move, set in motion [敎動]

sentences.t: Žürčedei basa Doṅγaid-i daruba.
sentences.l: Žürčedei again Doṅγaid-(object) overcame.
sentences.i: Jürchedei overcame the Dongqaid in turn.
sentences.n: basa is 'again, also' (Ming 再). The short unit is the third victory in a row; the Mongol keeps the same verb, daruba.

sentences.t: Daružu aisuqui-dur Qori-Šilemün-Taiži miṅγan turγaγ̇ud(i)-jar dobtulba.
sentences.l: Having-overcome coming-when Qori-Šilemün-Taiži thousand guards-with leading charged.
sentences.i: Having overcome them, as he came on, Qori-Shilemün Taiji charged, leading the Thousand Guards.
sentences.n: turγaγ̇ud(i)-jar is the guards with -jar 'leading, with', as before with the tribe names (Ming 護衞(每)領着). Miṅγan turγaγ̇ud is the Thousand Guards of unit 28, so the order of battle has been kept. dobtulba closes it.

morph.gloss: Qori-Shilemün Taiji, a man's name with the title taiži 'prince' [人名]

sentences.t: Žürčedei basa Qori-Šilemün- Taiži-ji ičuγ̇ažu daružu aisuqui-dur
sentences.l: Žürčedei again Qori-Šilemün Taiži-(object) causing-to-withdraw, having-overcome, coming-when,
sentences.i: Jürchedei again drove Qori-Shilemün Taiji back, and having overcome him, as he came on,
sentences.n: The name Qori-Šilemün-Taiži is broken across the line (Qori-Šilemün- / Taiži-ji), two words in print. ičuγ̇ažu is 'making withdraw' (Ming 敎退着), the stem inferred: ič- 'retreat' + causative -uγ̇a- + -žu. The clause ends in aisuqui-dur, 'when coming', and is completed in the next two units.

morph.gloss: Qori-Shilemün, first part of a name, broken across the line (hyphen) [人名]
taiži, prince (second part of the name) [行]
to make withdraw (ič- 'retreat' + causative -uγ̇a-, stem inferred) [敎退着]

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān-(n)ača eje ügeiġü Seṅgüm esergü dobtulqu bolun
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān-from counsel without Seṅgüm facing charging being,
sentences.i: without taking counsel with Wang Qan, Senggum, bent on charging to meet them,
sentences.n: Waṅ-Qān-(n)ača is Wang Qan with the ablative -ača (Ming 處), 'from Wang Qan'; eje ügeiġü is 'counsel without' (Ming 商量 無), 'without consulting'. dobtulqu bolun is the participle dobtulqu with bol- 'become' + -un, 'wanting to charge, bent on charging' (with the Ming 要 'wish to', and as in bailduqu bolun, 'about to give battle', of an earlier part)

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名 處]
Senggum, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to become, to be (dobtulqu bolun, 'about to charge'; Ming 要 'wish to') [要]

sentences.t: eṅgesge Qačar(i)-jan qaγdažu Seṅgüm mün tende unažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Red cheek-own being-shot, Seṅgüm just there had-fallen.
sentences.i: and was shot in the ruddy cheek; Senggum fell on the spot.
sentences.n: eṅgesge is Ming 紅, 'red'; with qačar 'cheek' (Ming 腮) the sense is 'his red cheek', but the order is odd and I cannot say what eṅgesge does. qaγdažu is qaγ- 'shoot' + passive -da- + -žu, 'being shot' (Ming 被射着), the stem inferred. unažuγ̇u is una- 'fall' + the past -žuγ̇u (Ming 倒了有). mün tende is 'right there'. Seṅgüm is Wang Qan's son (Ming 人名).

morph.gloss: to shoot (stem inferred from the Ming 射) [被射着]

sentences.t: Seṅgüm-i unaγdažu Kereid büġüdeġer Seṅgüm-ün deġere egeġerčü baiba.
sentences.l: Seṅgüm-(object) being-felled, Kereid all Seṅgüm-of on turning-over, stood.
sentences.i: With Senggum felled, the Kereid all wheeled round over him and stood.
sentences.n: unaγdažu is una- + -γda- + -žu, 'being felled' (Ming 被倒着), the accusative on Seṅgüm-i going with the passive as the Ming reads it. büġüdeġer is büġüde 'all' + -ġer 'by', used as an adverb (Ming 都). egeġerčü is the same verb as in unit 63, now with the converb -čü; Seṅgüm-ün deġere, 'on Senggum', parallels Quildar-un deġere there. baiba is 'stood'.

morph.gloss: the Kereid, a people (the -d is probably plural) [種(名)]
instrumental, used as an adverb: all together
Senggum, a man's name [人名 的]
to turn back, wheel about (Ming 翻 'turn over'; the ü drops before the ending) [翻着]

sentences.t: An-i daružu šiṅgeküi naran Quburi deġere tašin büküi-dür
sentences.l: Them having-overcome, setting sun Quburi on striking being-when,
sentences.i: Having overcome them, as the setting sun was striking the hill Quburi,
sentences.n: An-i is the oblique stem an- 'them' (third person plural, inferred) + accusative (Ming 他每行). šiṅgeküi naran is 'setting sun' (Ming 落的 日). Quburi is a low hill (Ming 低山), deġere 'on it'. tašin büküi-dür is taši- 'strike, pat' (inferred from the Ming 拍着) + -n and büküi-dür 'when being'; 'striking' is the Ming's word and I hold it loosely, since I can't say whether the sun is 'on' or 'touching' the hill.

morph.gloss: them (third-person plural oblique stem, inferred; compare teden-, teġün-) [他每行]
hill, rise of ground (Ming 低山) [低山]
to strike, pat (stem inferred from the Ming 拍着, sense uncertain) [拍着]

sentences.t: bidan-uγ̇ai egeġerčü Quildar-i umaγsan jaratu-ji abuγ̇ad qarižu
sentences.l: Ours turning, Quildar-(object) fallen wounded-(object) having-taken, turning-back,
sentences.i: our men wheeled round, took up the fallen Quildar, who was wounded, and turned back;
sentences.n: bidan-uγ̇ai is bidan-u, 'our' (unit 30), with an ending -γ̇ai (Ming 俺的 here, 咱的 in the next unit), used for 'our side'; the narrator says 'ours' about Chinggis's men. umaγsan is una- 'fall' + participle -γsan (Ming 倒了的); the Han 兀納黑三 reads unaγsan, so Shiratori's m is a misprint. jaratu-ji is jara 'wound' + -tu 'having' + -ji (Ming 傷有的 行), the having-pattern again, 'the one having a wound'. abuγ̇ad is 'having taken', qarižu 'turning back'.

morph.gloss: ending of uncertain force: ours (Ming 咱的)
to turn back, wheel about (Ming 翻 'turn over'; the ü drops before the ending) [翻着]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan bidan-uγ̇ai Waṅ-Qān-(n)ača qadqulduγsan γažar-ača qaγačažu üdeši-de ködölžü qaγačan qonoba.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan ours Waṅ-Qān-from fought-where place-from separating, evening-in moving, apart spent-the-night.
sentences.i: Our Chinggis Qahan left the place where they had fought Wang Qan, moved off in the evening, and passed the night apart from them.
sentences.n: qadqulduγsan γažar-ača is 'from the place where (they) had fought', the participle -γsan + γažar 'place' + ablative -ača. qaγačažu and qaγačan are both qaγača- 'part from, separate' (Ming 分離着, 分離): once as a converb, then as -n. üdeši-de is 'in the evening' (Ming 晩行). qonoba is qono- 'pass the night' + past -ba, the finite verb that finally ends the chain. The section stops at the night camp. bidan-uγ̇ai (Ming 咱的) stands beside Čiṅgis Qaγan, so 'Our Chinggis Qahan' is a loose rendering of 'Chinggis Qahan, ours'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin [太祖︀]
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid [人名 處]
